The dish is a white bowl about 15 cm across, holding what looks like yogurt or a creamy sauce such as mayonnaise or sour cream. The pile is roughly 9 cm across and about 3 to 4 cm deep, so it is a modest serving.

Treating the pile as a dome of about 9 cm diameter and 3.5 cm height, its volume is roughly (π/6)·h·(3a² + h²) with a = 4.5 cm. That gives about 0.5236 × 3.5 × (60.75 + 12.25) ≈ 134 mL. I'll round to about 150 g, since the pile may sit partly below the rim.

The type of food changes the energy a lot. Plain yogurt is about 60 kcal per 100 g, which would give about 90 kcal. Full-fat or Greek yogurt is nearer 100 kcal per 100 g. The glossy, thick look could also fit sour cream (about 200 kcal per 100 g) or mayonnaise (about 700 kcal per 100 g). It looks most like yogurt, perhaps a thick full-fat one, so I'll take about 110 kcal per 100 g, which comes to about 165 kcal for 150 g.
